newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street stocks seen higher after CPI.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street stocks seen higher after CPI.

text.p: Wall Street stocks are expected to head higher at the opening on Wednesday after U.S. consumer price data for September was as expected and sparked some upward movement in the bond market.
Still, analysts said they thought the stock market would have to retrench before any further rally after its dramatic surge past 6,000 on the Dow Jones industrial average on Monday.
"The data bode well for the market," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co. "This will take the sting out of the downward move that the street may be expecting."

The consumer price index rose 0.3 percent with an equal increase in the core rate which excludes food and energy. U.S. Treasuries rallied on the news though the long bond quickly slashed its gains and was up 1/32 to yield 6.84 percent.

"The market will need some time to retrench after crossing 6000 on the Dow," Ackerman said, and other analysts pointed out that even solid earnings reports might not be enough to force a rally after the recent upward move.
Analysts said that little decisive action was likely ahead of Thursday's September housing starts and industrial production and capacity utilization.
